title: fix-network deployment diagram
description: How fix-network runs: a binary installed on the Mac it diagnoses, started from a terminal by a developer or a coding agent, that runs macOS's network commands (some through sudo), probes the network, and may leave a detached Wi-Fi watchdog behind.

nodes.name: Developer's terminal
nodes.description: Runs diagnose or fix and answers sudo's password prompt.

nodes.name: Coding agent's shell
nodes.description: Runs the same commands for the developer, as agents/skills/fix-network/SKILL.md says; privileged steps still use the developer's terminal sudo.
nodes.condition: When a coding agent follows the fix-network skill.

nodes.name: The developer's Mac
nodes.description: The machine being diagnosed and repaired. Any other OS is refused with exit status 2.

nodes.name: fix-network
nodes.description: One run of diagnose or fix; writes its log and original settings to a private state directory under $FIXNET_STATE or ~/.local/state/fix-network.

nodes.name: macOS network commands
nodes.description: networksetup, scutil, ifconfig, netstat, route, ipconfig, sysctl, sw_vers, ping, dig and curl, each run with a time limit; dscacheutil, killall, arp, ipconfig set, route flush and proxy changes run through sudo.

nodes.name: Wi-Fi watchdog (recover.sh)
nodes.description: A detached /bin/sh script in its own process group that turns Wi-Fi back on after 45 seconds.

nodes.name: Apple captive-portal check and website
nodes.description: captive.apple.com/hotspot-detect.html over HTTP to detect a captive portal; www.apple.com resolved through the system resolver and fetched over HTTPS.

nodes.name: Public IP probe address
nodes.description: 1.1.1.1 when the link has an IPv4 address, and 2606:4700:4700::1111 when it has a global IPv6 address, reached by TCP on port 443 to test the raw IP path.

nodes.name: Router (gateway)
nodes.description: The gateway of the service in use, from ipconfig getoption; pinged to tell a dead router from an upstream outage, and its ARP entry cleared as a repair step.
nodes.condition: When the service in use has an IPv4 gateway.

nodes.name: Configured DNS servers
nodes.description: The primary or split-DNS server, asked directly with dig.
nodes.condition: When a lookup through the system resolver fails.

nodes.name: Internal hosts
nodes.description: The hosts named with --internal-host: resolved, routed and, with a port, connected to by TCP.

nodes.name: System proxies and PAC file
nodes.description: The enabled HTTP and HTTPS proxies (TCP) and the PAC URL (curl).
nodes.condition: Only when the Mac has system proxies or a PAC file set.

artifacts.name: fix-network
artifacts.description: Built with cargo build --release -p fix-network, or installed from the universal macOS release tarball or the zazzle Homebrew formula; zazzle fix-network ... runs the same binary from beside the zazzle invoker.
